text: 2 Applicability The goal of this measure is to achieve 5% duct air leakage combined with R-8 insulation for ducts located in unconditioned spaces. Ducts in the conditioned spaces do not require treatment because their heat loss goes directly to the conditioned space and is therefore not “wasted”. This measure applies to dwelling units with either duct leakage to the outside greater than 6% or duct insulation less than R-6. Dwelling units with 0% leakage and uninsulated ducts are not included, as these configurations typically indicate that the ducts are located entirely within conditioned spaces and ResStock reflects this assumption. Though, ducts in real homes can pass through both conditioned and unconditioned spaces, requiring section-by-section treatment. Nevertheless, based on these assumptions, this duct sealing and insulation measure applies to approximately 46.3% of the U.S. housing stock, as shown in Table 1. Table 1. This measure does not change whether ducts are present or their locations; it only changes the duct insulation and leakage. Air leakage and heat gains and losses are calculated for the fraction of the ductwork outside conditioned space. The primary location of the duct system is sampled from the ‘duct location.tsv’ file.
